title: git-cicd verdict is present and pending from the moment the workflow starts
body:
Unit 3 of plan `mdci-dev-6692` (record: `.pearls/docs/epics/mdci-dev-6692.md` in `mangimangi/medici-dev`). Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27: "I agree we should fix...I think pending w status write is ok".

## What happens today

The interface git-cicd was built to says: "One always-present check with a fixed name ... so anything waiting on 'checks pass' is never left hanging", and that "nothing ran" is never read as "passed". In v0.0.1 the check `git-cicd verdict` is the **last** thing to appear on a pull request. The generated workflow (`templates/workflow.yml`) is `decide`, then one runner per needed job, then `verdict`; GitHub creates a check run for a job only when that job is queued, and `verdict` is queued after the others finish. Between `decide` finishing and the job runners being queued, every check that exists on the commit is green.

That window was hit on the first repository to adopt git-cicd. On medici #177 (2026-11-27), medici's walker waited for the pull request's checks, saw "1 reported, none failed or pending" (the vendor-file check), and merged at about 16:15:40 UTC. `git-cicd decide` finished at 16:15:46; `unit-tests` and `toolchain-contract` started at 16:15:48; `git-cicd verdict` finished green at 16:20:24, four and a half minutes after the merge. Any reader that merges when no check is failing or pending can do the same on any repository that uses git-cicd.

The same window exists when no job is needed, and when `decide` itself has not started yet.

## Required behaviour

From the moment the git-cicd workflow starts on a pull request, something named `git-cicd verdict` is on the pull request's head commit and is **pending**, and it stays pending until the verdict is known. It then becomes success or failure exactly as the verdict is today (failed when a blocking job failed or could not run, or when the workflow does not match the config; otherwise passed, including when no job was needed). At no moment after the workflow has started is every check on the commit green while the verdict is still to come. A workflow run that is cancelled or superseded, or that dies before the verdict, does not leave `git-cicd verdict` green.

The owner accepted the cost: on the `open` moment the workflow's token may write commit statuses, as a narrow exception to "read-only on `open`". It gets that one write permission and no other; contents stay read-only. Nothing else about the interface changes: only the cron block of the generated file varies with the config; `verify` still compares the whole file; every fact about the change still reaches the tool as an environment variable.

A reader must not be shown two things of the same name that disagree: if both a status and a check run carry the name `git-cicd verdict`, they never show one green while the other is pending, and the documentation says which one a reader (a person, branch protection, a script that lists a pull request's checks) should rely on.

If this cannot be had with GitHub Actions as required, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was found; do not ship something that narrows the window without closing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- On this issue's own pull request into `plan/mdci-dev-6692`, `git-cicd verdict` is pending on the head commit before git-cicd's `test` job has finished, and ends green; the pull request description gives the evidence (timestamps of the pending state and of the `test` job, read from the platform, not asserted).
- With no job needed (a change only to files in `needs_nothing`), `git-cicd verdict` is pending from the start of the run and ends green with the "0 of N jobs needed" text.
- When a blocking job fails, `git-cicd verdict` ends failed.
- The generated workflow grants, on the pull request trigger, the status-write permission and no other write permission; a test asserts the permissions block.
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` still generate the same file, and `verify` still fails on a hand edit.
- `README.md` says the verdict is present and pending from the start, names the permission and why, and says which object a reader should wait on.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; the checks on this issue's pull request are seen green, including `git-cicd verdict`, before the work is called done.
- git-cicd's own `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed with the change.

## Out of scope

The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any change to git-vendored or git-semver, or to a vendor-protected file. Any change in medici or another consumer: they pick the fix up by installing the release and regenerating their workflow.

title: The pending git-cicd verdict is posted without waiting for a superseded run to be cancelled
body:
Follow-up to `gcd-f8eb` (git-cicd #5), unit 3 of plan `mdci-dev-6692`. This issue's branch starts from `gcd-f8eb/impl`, so its pull request contains #5 and replaces it. Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27.

## What happens today

With #5, `git-cicd verdict` is a commit status that the first step of the first job (`git-cicd decide`) sets to pending. #5 states: "Until that first step runs, the `git-cicd decide` check run is itself queued. So the commit never shows only green checks while the verdict is still to come."

That does not hold when a run is superseding an older one. The generated workflow has a workflow-level `concurrency` group per pull request with `cancel-in-progress` on pull requests, so a newer run waits, with no job created and therefore no check run and no status, until the older run has been cancelled.

This is what was hit on medici #177 (2026-11-27), read from `GET /repos/mangimangi/medici/actions/runs/46032007325/jobs` and the run list:

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 16:14:53 | git-cicd run 46031961919 created on `f090b1d` |
| 16:15:10 | a second push; git-cicd run 46032007325 created on `450267a`; Check Vendor Files run created |
| 16:15:21 | `check` (Check Vendor Files, a separate workflow) completed, success |
| 16:15:37 | run 46031961919 finished cancelling; **`git-cicd decide` job of run 46032007325 created** |
| 16:15:39 | `git-cicd decide` started |
| ~16:15:40 | medici's walker, having read "1 reported, none failed or pending", merged the pull request |
| 16:20:24 | the verdict, green |

From 16:15:21 to 16:15:37 the head commit had exactly one check, and it was green. A pending status posted by the first step of `decide` would have appeared at about 16:15:40.

## Required behaviour

When a git-cicd run starts for a head commit, the pending `git-cicd verdict` status is posted without waiting for any other run of the workflow to finish or be cancelled. Superseding is kept where it saves work: a newer push still cancels the older run's jobs that run the repository's scripts. A superseded or cancelled run never turns the newer commit's status green, and never leaves its own commit's status green without a verdict. Everything #5 established stays: one object named `git-cicd verdict`, the status; `statuses: write` only on the jobs that post it; only the cron block of the generated file varies; `verify` compares the whole file.

`README.md` is corrected where it repeats the claim above: it says what a reader can rely on and from when, including the superseding case, and does not promise more than the platform gives (the short time between a push and GitHub creating the run is the platform's).

If GitHub Actions cannot post the status ahead of the concurrency wait, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was tried.

## Acceptance criteria

- Shown on this issue's own pull request, with times read from the platform and given in the pull request description: two pushes to the pull request less than 30 seconds apart; for the second run, the time the run was created, the time its status-posting job was created, and the time `git-cicd verdict` became pending on the second head commit. The pending status is there within a few seconds of the run being created, not after the first run has finished cancelling.
- In that same sequence the first run's script-running job is cancelled (superseding still works), and the first commit's `git-cicd verdict` does not end green unless its verdict really was reached.
- The second commit's `git-cicd verdict` ends green.
- A test asserts where the concurrency group is and is not in the generated workflow, and the permissions block is unchanged from #5 (status write on the posting jobs only).
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; git-cicd's own `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed; the checks and the status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

Readers of checks (`madp pr checks`, medici's merge step): they are other repositories' work. The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any vendor-protected file.

title: Checks say whose they are: a job's display name, repo:job rows, and owner@version per step in the report
body:
Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27. The owner: "would be nice if the git-cicd checks had format `<human readable name> / <owning repo>:<job name>:<step name>`", and "owning repo should incl version...it should be clear jobs repo version".

## What happens today

On a pull request in a repository that uses git-cicd v0.0.2 (medici, for example) the rows are `git-cicd decide`, one row per job named with the bare job name from the config (`unit-tests`, `toolchain-contract`), and `git-cicd report`, each shown by GitHub after the workflow's name (`git-cicd / unit-tests`), plus the commit status `git-cicd verdict`. A job has no display name: `templates/workflow.yml` names the script-running job `${{ matrix.job }}`. A step is named only in the report, and only when it fails (`failed (step <step>, exit <code>)`). Nothing says which repository a step's script belongs to, or which version of a vendored tool ran.

## Required behaviour

1. **A job may declare a display name**, the optional field `name` in the config (a short human-readable string). It is validated like every other field; a job without one behaves as if its `name` were its job name. `README.md`, `templates/config.schema` and the default config template know the field.

2. **Rows are stable and say whose job it is.** The script-running job's row is `<name> / <repo>:<job>`, where `<repo>` is the name of the repository the workflow runs in (for example `Unit tests / medici:unit-tests`). No version appears in a row name: a row name is what branch protection and anything else that waits on a check refers to, and it must not change when a tool is upgraded. `git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd report` and the status `git-cicd verdict` keep their names.

3. **The report names every step, with its owner and the owner's version.** For each job the report has one line per step that ran (and setup), in the form `<name> / <owner>@<version>:<job>:<step>`, with its result and its time; the job's own line stays. `<step>` is the step's file name. `<owner>` is the vendor when the step's file is under `.vendored/pkg/<vendor>/`, with `<version>` read from `.vendored/manifests/<vendor>.version`; otherwise the owner is the repository itself, with the version from the version file the repository's git-semver config names (`.vendored/configs/git-semver.json`, `version_file`, default `VERSION`) when that file exists. An owner with no version is shown without `@<version>`; a version is never guessed. The verdict status's description stays within the platform's length limit; the step lines belong to the report.

4. **A pull request tests a change, not a release.** The report's header gives the short head commit, so the repository's own version (the last release) is not read as the version of the change under test.

5. The same names appear in a local run (`git-cicd check`), where the repository's name comes from the checkout (say how, and what is shown when it cannot be found).

The injection rules hold: a display name is data. It reaches the workflow only through the decide job's outputs and environment variables, never spliced into a command line, and a name containing quotes, `$`, backticks or a newline is either refused at validation or shown literally and runs nothing. Only the cron block of the generated file varies with the config; `verify` still compares the whole file.

If the row name cannot carry the display name without the generated file varying with the config, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`).

## Acceptance criteria

- A config with `"name"` on a job validates; a `name` that is not a non-empty single-line string is refused with the job and the reason; a job without `name` is unchanged apart from the new row format.
- On this issue's own pull request, git-cicd's own job shows as `<name> / git-cicd:test` (its config gains a `name`), read from the platform and quoted in the pull request description.
- The report for a job with a repository step and a step under `.vendored/pkg/<vendor>/` shows both lines with the right owner and version; tests cover a vendored owner with a manifest version, a vendored owner without one, the repository with a version file, and the repository without one.
- A test shows a display name with shell metacharacters reaches the report unaltered and runs nothing.
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` (their `name` included) still generate the same workflow file.
- `README.md` documents the field, the row format, the report's step lines and where each version comes from.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed if the template changed; the checks and the `git-cicd verdict` status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

A row or a status per step. Versions in row names. The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any vendor-protected file. Consumers: they pick this up by installing the release and regenerating their workflow.

title: git-cicd's own rows and status follow the naming pattern; one workflow per moment, named for it; title-case names
body:
Follow-up to `gcd-8b02` (git-cicd #8). This issue's branch starts from `gcd-8b02/impl`, so its pull request contains #8 and replaces it. Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27, after seeing #8's rows on the platform.

## What happens today (with #8)

On a pull request the rows are, as GitHub shows them: `git-cicd / git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd / Unit tests / git-cicd:test`, `git-cicd / git-cicd report`, and the status `git-cicd verdict`.

- The job rows follow `<name> / <repo>:<job>`; `git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd report` and the status `git-cicd verdict` do not. The owner: "how come decide, verdict and report don't follow the naming pattern?" (The planning session had told #8 to leave them.)
- GitHub puts the workflow's name before every row, and the one generated workflow is named `git-cicd` for every moment. The owner: "I see git-cicd before the human readable name".
- A job without `name` shows its bare job name (`unit-tests`), and git-cicd's own config says `"name": "Unit tests"`. The owner: "the human readable name should be title case".
- There is one generated file, `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml`, for all four moments. Permissions by moment (read-only on `open`; write on `merge`, `cron` and manual) and the overlap rules (`open` superseded; `merge` queued, never cancelled) would all be conditions inside it.

## Required behaviour

1. **git-cicd's own rows and status follow the pattern, with git-cicd as their owner.** The deciding job's row is `Decide / git-cicd:decide`, the reporting job's is `Report / git-cicd:report`, and the commit status is `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`. Everything #5 and #6 established about the status holds under its new name: one object carries the name; pending from the first step of the first job, without waiting on a superseded run; final from the last step of the report job; a cancelled or superseded run never leaves it green.

2. **One generated workflow per moment, named for the moment.** The workflow for the `open` moment is named `Open`, so a row reads `Open / Unit Tests / medici:unit-tests`. The names for the others are `Merge`, `Cron` and `Manual`; the owner chose the moment words over `CI`/`CD` because the config already says `"on": ["open"]` and a moment is not a kind of job. Each moment's workflow is its own file with its own trigger, its own permissions stated at the top level or per job, and its own overlap rule. **Only the `open` file is generated in this issue**, because only `open` executes; the generator, `verify`, the README and the tests are shaped so that adding the `merge`, `cron` and manual files later adds files and changes none. Choose the file names once, so no adopter has to rename a file again, and record them. The rule "only the cron block varies with the config" becomes: every generated file is fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block.

3. **The old single file goes.** `generate` in a repository that has `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` writes the new file and removes the old one; `verify` fails, naming the command to run, while the old file is still there or the new one is missing or different. `install.sh` lists the generated workflow files as editable for the vendor check in a way that covers the files to come. git-cicd's own repository is migrated in this issue.

4. **Title case, by convention and by default, never by rewriting.** A job without `name` is shown under a name derived from its job name: `-` and `_` become spaces and each word is capitalised (`unit-tests` shows as `Unit Tests`). A `name` a repository wrote is shown exactly as written; git-cicd does not change its case (`PyPI`, `mypy`). git-cicd's own config and every example in the README, the schema description and the tests use title case.

Everything else stands: rows carry no version; the report's step lines are `<name> / <owner>@<version>:<job>:<step>`; a display name is data and runs nothing; `statuses: write` only on the jobs that post the status and no other write permission on `open`.

If GitHub does not allow something here as required (for example a row or status name in this form), stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was tried.

## Acceptance criteria

- On this issue's own pull request, read from the platform and quoted in the description: the check runs `Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `Unit Tests / git-cicd:test` and `Report / git-cicd:report`, under the workflow named `Open`; the commit status `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`, pending before the test job finishes and ending success; no check or status named `git-cicd decide`, `git-cicd report` or `git-cicd verdict` on the head commit.
- `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` no longer exists in this repository; the `open` workflow file does and is the generator's output; `verify` passes, and fails in a test when the old file is present.
- A job without `name` is shown as its job name in title case, in the row and in the report; a job with `name` is shown exactly as written (tests for both, including a mixed-case name).
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` generate the same files.
- A test asserts the `open` workflow's permissions: status write on the two posting jobs only, nothing on the job that runs scripts.
- `README.md` describes the per-moment workflows and their names, the file names, the migration from the single file (`generate`, commit the new file and the deletion), the rows and the status under their new names, and which object a reader waits on.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; the checks and the status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

Executing `merge`, `cron` or manual runs, and generating their files. A row or status per step. Versions in row names. Any vendor-protected file. Consumers: medici names `git-cicd verdict` in its docs and has `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml`; it migrates when it installs the release, in its own repository.

title: Moments are called triggers: CICD_TRIGGER, --trigger, and the docs
body:
Follow-up to `gcd-f7ce` (git-cicd #9). This issue's branch starts from `gcd-f7ce/impl`, so its pull request contains #8 and #9 and replaces both. The owner, 2026-11-27: "moment is really trigger...is it too late to change that?"

## What happens today

git-cicd calls `open`, `merge`, `cron` and a manual run "moments". The word is not in a repository's config (the field is `on`), but it is everywhere else: about 95 places in `git-cicd`, `README.md`, the workflow templates and the tests. Two of them are public: the environment variable `CICD_MOMENT` every setup and step script receives, and the `--moment` option of `decide`, `run-job` and `report`. Messages say "the <moment> moment is not built yet". Nothing outside this repository depends on the word yet: medici, the only adopter, does not read `CICD_MOMENT` and does not use the term.

## Required behaviour

The word is "trigger" everywhere a person or a script meets it, and nothing is left that says "moment" in this sense:

- Scripts receive `CICD_TRIGGER`; `CICD_MOMENT` is no longer set.
- The commands take `--trigger`; `--moment` is not accepted.
- Messages, the report, the README, the schema descriptions, comments in the generated workflows, and the code's own identifiers and tests use "trigger" ("the merge trigger is not built yet").
- No alias and no deprecation path: the owner chose not to keep a second name, because nothing uses the first.

Nothing else changes: the config field stays `on` with the values `open`, `merge`, `cron`; the workflows are still named `Open`, `Merge`, `Cron`, `Manual`, one file per trigger; rows, the `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` status, permissions and the generated file names are as #9 left them. If the generated workflow's text changes, it is regenerated and committed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `git grep -i moment` in this repository finds nothing in `git-cicd`, `README.md`, `templates/`, `tests/`, `ci/`, `install.sh` or `.github/workflows/` that uses the word for a trigger (an ordinary English use, if any is left, is listed in the pull request description).
- A test shows a step receives `CICD_TRIGGER=open` and that `CICD_MOMENT` is absent from its environment.
- `--moment` is rejected as an unknown option; `--trigger` works on every command that took `--moment`.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; `verify` passes; the checks and the `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` status on this pull request are seen green before the work is called done.

## Out of scope

Any change of behaviour. The tracker's and planning documents' history under `.pearls/` (they record what was said at the time). Executing `merge`, `cron` or manual runs.

title: Every trigger executes: merge, cron and manual runs, with declared inputs
Build the merge trigger: decide, run-job and report for a push, and the generated Merge workflow
body:
Epic gcd-bbdd, planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-bbdd.md (What ships: 'The merge trigger executes'). Delivers into plan/git-dev-883c. This issue lands first: the manual, declared-inputs, cron and own-jobs issues build on the non-pull-request verdict, the write permissions and the run queue it introduces.

## Current code (re-checked 2026-11-28, git-cicd v0.0.3)
- `GENERATED_TRIGGERS = ('open',)` at git-cicd:44; `WORKFLOWS` (git-cicd:38-43) already maps merge to (`Merge`, `.github/workflows/git-cicd-merge.yml`).
- `check_trigger` (git-cicd:403-414) raises `NOT_BUILT` (git-cicd:399: `the {trigger} trigger is not built yet (git-cicd gcd-e74c builds open only)`) for every trigger but open. It is called by `decide` (git-cicd:481), `run_job` (git-cicd:625) and `cmd_report` (git-cicd:1301).
- `decide` (git-cicd:481-550) already filters on `trigger not in job['on']` and on `branches` against `target`, and applies the forcing / paths / needs_nothing rules. `changed_files` (git-cicd:429) is `git diff --name-only --no-renames BASE...HEAD`.
- `script_env` (git-cicd:590-606) sets the CICD_ variables.
- install.sh: `TRIGGERS=(open)` (install.sh:40) decides which templates are downloaded and which generated files go into the manifest.
- Pattern to follow: templates/workflows/open.yml (header comment; decide / run / verdict jobs; the pending status as decide's first step; the final status as the report job's last step with `if: always()`; the `__TOOL__` placeholder; every fact passed through `env:`).

## Scope
1. `check_trigger` accepts merge. Cron and manual still exit 2 until their own issues. NOT_BUILT no longer names gcd-e74c; it says which triggers are built.
2. `decide`, `run-job` and `report` with `--trigger merge`. The needed jobs are those with merge in `on`, whose `branches` match `--target` (the branch the change landed on), and that the change affects, under the same paths / needs_nothing / forcing rules as open. The changed files are `changed_files(base, head)`, with base = the commit before the push.
3. DECISION: a push that creates a branch has an all-zero before sha (40 zeros). decide treats that, and any base that does not resolve, as 'cannot compute the diff', so every merge job whose branches match is needed, with that reason. Reason: the existing rule that a job is 'not needed' only on purpose.
4. CICD_ variables on merge: CICD_TRIGGER=merge; CICD_TARGET_BRANCH = the branch landed on; CICD_BASE = the commit before the push; CICD_HEAD = the landed commit (github.sha); CICD_CHANGED_FILES as on open. DECISION: CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH = the same branch as the target. Reason: a push has no separate source, and a script that reads the variable never sees it empty.
5. New templates/workflows/merge.yml, workflow name `Merge`, fixed text (only `__TOOL__` varies):
   - Event: `push` with `branches: ['**']` (every branch, no tags; the tool decides branches). DECISION: the jobs skip a push that deletes a branch (`github.event.deleted`). Reason: there is no commit to run on or to put a status on.
   - Permissions: top level `contents: read`. The decide and report jobs get `contents: read` and `statuses: write`, plus `actions: read` / `pull-requests: read` where the queue and pull-request checks below need them. The `run` job (the one that runs the config's scripts) gets `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`.
   - The run job checks out github.sha with `fetch-depth: 0` and `fetch-tags: true` (git-semver's release needs full history and tags).
   - Queue: runs on one branch go one at a time and are never cancelled. DECISION: merge.yml has no `concurrency` key at all. Reason: a GitHub concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false` still cancels a pending run when a newer one joins the group (it keeps one pending run per group), which would cancel a merge run. Instead, after posting pending, decide waits until no earlier run (lower run id) of a git-cicd write-trigger workflow (git-cicd-merge.yml and git-cicd-manual.yml, so a later manual release shares the queue) for the same branch is queued or in progress. It polls `gh api` on `repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs` with the branch passed as an env variable.
   - Verdict: the commit status `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` on the landed commit (github.sha). It is pending from decide's first step and final from the report job's last step (`if: always()`), and failure when the report did not run to the end, exactly as on open.
   - DECISION (collision with Open): a push to a branch with an open pull request triggers both Open and Merge on the same commit. Both would write the same status context and the last writer wins, so a Merge run that needs nothing could turn a failed Open verdict green. Rule: a non-open run (merge, and later manual and cron) posts the Verdict status, pending and final, only when no open pull request has that commit as its head (`gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$HEAD_SHA/pulls`, state open and head.sha equal). Otherwise its verdict is its `Report / git-cicd:report` check run, which fails on a FAILED verdict, plus its job summary, and the Open run owns the status. Reason: the owner's decision of 2026-11-27 makes the status the verdict 'when there is no pull request'. The README says so.
   - Rows as on open: `Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `<name> / <repo>:<job>`, `Report / git-cicd:report`. The only actions are actions/checkout@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4 and actions/download-artifact@v4. No `${{ }}` inside any `run:`.
   - A header comment like open.yml's, explaining the event, the permissions, the queue and the verdict.
6. `GENERATED_TRIGGERS` gains merge: `generate` writes git-cicd-merge.yml and `verify` covers it. DECISION: templates/workflows/open.yml is not touched, even though its header comment says merge is '(not built yet)'. Reason: the epic requires git-cicd-open.yml to stay byte-identical; the new templates' headers say what is generated.
7. install.sh: `TRIGGERS` gains merge, so the template is downloaded and the generated file is listed in the manifest.

title: Build manual runs: run one named job by hand through the generated Manual workflow
body:
Epic gcd-bbdd, planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-bbdd.md (What ships: 'Manual runs execute'). Delivers into plan/git-dev-883c. Depends on gcd-bbdd.1 (merge trigger), which provides the non-open verdict rule, the write permissions and the run queue that this issue reuses.

## Current code (re-checked 2026-11-28)
- `ALL_TRIGGERS = TRIGGERS + ('manual',)` (git-cicd:400) is used for the `--trigger` choices (`add_change_args`, git-cicd:1330-1336; `report --trigger`, git-cicd:1386).
- `check_trigger` (git-cicd:403-414) still refuses manual. It already names the jobs whose `manual` is true.
- `_validate_job` (git-cicd:198-332) normalizes `manual` (default true; `"manual": false` turns it off).
- `WORKFLOWS['manual']  = ('Manual', '.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml')` (git-cicd:42). `GENERATED_TRIGGERS` is at git-cicd:44. install.sh has `TRIGGERS=(...)` at install.sh:40.

## Scope
1. `check_trigger` accepts manual.
2. DECISION (interface): `decide --trigger manual` takes `--job NAME` (required with manual, refused with every other trigger). The other `--target/--source/--base/--head` arguments stay as they are.
   - The named job is needed when it exists, its `manual` is true and its `branches` match `--target` (the branch the run was started on). Its reason is 'manual run'. `paths` and needs_nothing are ignored.
   - Every other declared job is 'not needed (not the job asked for)'.
   - An unknown job (name the declared jobs), a job with `"manual": false`, or a branch that does not match the job's branches is a refusal. decide records it in the decision record (a `refused` field holding the reason), needs no job and exits 0, so the run reaches the report job. report then gives FAILED - <reason> in the report, the job summary and the status description.
   - Reason for the decision: the planning doc requires the reason to appear in the report, never silently.
   - `run_job` refuses the same cases (UsageError, exit 2) as a second guard.
3. DECISION: the CICD_ variables on manual are:
   - CICD_TRIGGER=manual
   - CICD_TARGET_BRANCH = CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH = the branch the run was started on (github.ref_name)
   - CICD_BASE = CICD_HEAD = the commit the run is for (github.sha)
   - CICD_CHANGED_FILES = an empty file

   Reason: a manual run has no change, and paths are ignored.
4. New templates/workflows/manual.yml, workflow name `Manual`, fixed text:
   - `on: workflow_dispatch` with one free-text input `job` (required, type string, with a description naming it as the config job to run).
   - The input reaches the tool only through `env:` (for example `JOB: ${{ inputs.job }}`), never as `${{ }}` inside `run:`.
   - Permissions as on Merge: write (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`) on the job that runs the config's scripts; `statuses: write` and what the queue needs on decide and report.
   - The same queue step as Merge, so manual and merge runs on one branch go one at a time and are never cancelled (version-bump.yml today shares the group push-to-main between push and dispatch). If gcd-bbdd.1 already lists git-cicd-manual.yml among the queued workflows, nothing changes there.
   - The run job checks out github.sha with `fetch-depth: 0` and `fetch-tags: true`.
   - Verdict: `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` on github.sha, pending first and final last, under the same no-open-pull-request rule as Merge.
   - A header comment in the style of open.yml.
5. `GENERATED_TRIGGERS` and install.sh `TRIGGERS` gain manual. Commit the generated .github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml. git-cicd-open.yml stays byte-identical.
6. Local `check` is unchanged; it stays on open.

## Tests (extend the existing files, following their patterns)
- tests/test_decide.py: a manual run of a job; unknown job; `"manual": false`; a branch mismatch; paths ignored; `--job` refused for other triggers.
- tests/test_run.py: the manual CICD_ variables and the run_job refusals.
- tests/test_report.py: a refusal gives FAILED with the reason, and verdict-out carries it.
- tests/test_workflow.py:
  - the manual file is written, is named `Manual`, and has a `workflow_dispatch` with the `job` input;
  - no `${{ }}` in `run:`;
  - permissions;
  - pending first and final last;
  - verify fails on a hand edit;
  - the file-name test is updated.
- tests/test_install.py.

## Docs
- README.md:
  - 'What is built today';
  - 'When a job runs' gains a manual bullet: on unless `"manual": false`, branches bind, paths are ignored;
  - 'What a script is given' (manual meanings);
  - 'The generated workflows' table, plus a 'The manual workflow (Manual)' section on how to start one from the Actions tab;
  - the Commands table (`decide --job`);
  - 'Not built yet'.
- AGENTS.md: the list of generated workflows.

## Acceptance criteria
- `decide`, `run-job` and `report` run with `--trigger manual`. An unknown job, `"manual": false`, or a non-matching branch fails the run with the reason in the report, never silently.
- `generate` writes git-cicd-manual.yml, `verify` covers it, and git-cicd-open.yml stays byte-identical.
- The `job` input never appears as `${{ }}` inside `run:`.
- The suite passes on Python 3.11, `./git-cicd check` passes, and `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/<pr target>` reports nothing.

title: Declared inputs for manual runs: a job declares its inputs, steps get them as CICD_INPUT_ environment variables
body:
Epic gcd-bbdd, planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-bbdd.md (What ships: 'Declared inputs for manual runs'). Delivers into plan/git-dev-883c. Depends on gcd-bbdd.2 (manual runs) for the Manual workflow, `decide --trigger manual --job` and the refusal-in-report path.

## Current code (re-checked 2026-11-28)
- `JOB_FIELDS` (git-cicd:59-60) lists the allowed job fields. Unknown fields are refused in `_validate_job` (git-cicd:198-332), which returns the normalized job.
- `script_env` (git-cicd:590-606) builds a step's environment. `run_job` is at git-cicd:625.
- templates/config.schema holds the `jobs` description string that lists every job field.

## Design (DECISIONS, recorded here and in the planning doc)
1. Job field `inputs`: an object mapping an input name to a declaration. Names match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. A declaration has:
   - `description`: optional single-line printable string;
   - `required`: boolean, default false;
   - `default`: string;
   - `choices`: a non-empty array of distinct strings.

   Every value is a string. A boolean such as git-vendored's `private` is a choice of `true` and `false`. Reason: values reach scripts as environment variables, which are strings.
2. A required input may not have a default. Reason: a default would make `required` meaningless. Inputs that GitHub declares as required with a default today (`bump_type`) are declared as not required with that default, which carries the same behaviour.
3. `validate` refuses a malformed declaration, naming the job and the reason, in the style of the existing errors (`job X: input Y: ...`). That covers:
   - a bad name;
   - an unknown key;
   - a non-string default or description;
   - a default outside the choices;
   - empty, duplicate or non-string choices;
   - `required` that is not a boolean, or that is set together with a default;
   - `inputs` that is not an object.
4. Naming rule: every declared input reaches every step and the setup as `CICD_INPUT_<NAME upper-cased>` (bump_type becomes CICD_INPUT_BUMP_TYPE). It is always set: to the manual value, else the default, else the empty string. Inherited `CICD_INPUT_*` variables the job does not declare are removed from the script's environment.
5. Carrying values through a fixed workflow: templates/workflows/manual.yml gains a second fixed free-text `workflow_dispatch` input, `inputs` (not required, default empty). It holds a JSON object of string values, for example {bump_type: minor} written as JSON with double-quoted keys and values.
   - It reaches the tool only as the `env:` entry `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS: ${{ inputs.inputs }}` on the decide and run steps. The tool reads it from the environment for `--trigger manual`; it is never a command-line argument and never `${{ }}` inside `run:`.
   - An empty value means {}.
   - CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS is removed from the scripts' environment, so the per-input variables are the only channel.
   - Reason: the generated file must not vary with the config's jobs, so it cannot list per-job inputs. GitHub also caps the number of dispatch inputs. JSON carries quotes and newlines exactly.
6. A manual run fails with the reason, refused in decide and reported FAILED as in gcd-bbdd.2, and run-job re-checks, when:
   - the JSON is invalid or not an object of strings;
   - an input is undeclared;
   - a required input is missing;
   - a value is outside the choices.
7. Every other trigger (open, merge, cron and local `check`) gives a step the declared defaults (or the empty string).

## Must carry today's workflows
Show in tests that these declarations validate and run:
- version-bump.yml: `bump_type` (choices patch, minor, major; default patch), `subdirectory`, `changelog_description`.
- install-vendored.yml: `vendor` (default all), `version` (default latest), `private` (choices true, false; default false).
- git-vendored's validate: `repo`, `version`.

## Tests (follow tests/test_config.py, tests/test_run.py, tests/test_decide.py, tests/test_workflow.py)
- One validate error per malformed case above.
- A manual value containing single and double quotes, `$`, backticks and a newline reaches a step literally. The step script writes `CICD_INPUT_X` to a file, and the test compares the bytes.
- Defaults on open and merge; undeclared inherited CICD_INPUT_ variables are dropped.
- Each failure case gives a refusal with its reason.
- manual.yml has the `inputs` input and no `${{ }}` in `run:`.
- git-cicd-open.yml stays byte-identical.

## Docs
- README.md:
  - the 'A job declares' table gains `inputs`;
  - a new 'Declared inputs' section: the fields, the CICD_INPUT_ naming rule, the JSON in the Manual workflow's `inputs` field, the defaults on other triggers, and the failures;
  - 'What a script is given';
  - 'No accidental injection';
  - the Manual workflow section;
  - 'Not built yet' drops declared inputs.
- templates/config.schema: the `jobs` description gains `inputs`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A job can declare inputs. `validate` refuses each malformed declaration, naming the job and the reason.
- Values reach steps only as CICD_INPUT_ environment variables. The tests show a value with quotes, `$`, backticks and a newline arriving literally.
- An undeclared input, a missing required one, or a value outside the choices fails the run with the reason.
- The generated workflows stay fixed text, and git-cicd-open.yml is byte-identical.
- The suite passes on Python 3.11, `./git-cicd check` passes, and `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/<pr target>` reports nothing.

title: Build the cron trigger: scheduled jobs run on their literal branches through the generated Cron workflow
body:
Epic gcd-bbdd, planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-bbdd.md (What ships: 'The cron trigger executes'). Delivers into plan/git-dev-883c. Depends on gcd-bbdd.1 (merge trigger) for the non-open verdict rule and the write-permission pattern.

## Current code (re-checked 2026-11-28)
- `schedule_block(config)` (git-cicd:711-718) already builds `  schedule:` with one `    - cron: <json string>` line per distinct, sorted expression, or an empty string when there are none.
- `render_workflow` (git-cicd:721-727) replaces the `__SCHEDULE__` line, which only a cron template holds. `test_schedule_block_fills_only_a_cron_template` and `test_cron_jobs_do_not_change_the_open_file` (tests/test_workflow.py) cover that.
- `_validate_job` already requires `cron` (five fields) exactly when `on` contains cron, and literal `branches` for cron jobs (git-cicd:263-283).
- `WORKFLOWS['cron'] = ('Cron', '.github/workflows/git-cicd-cron.yml')`. `GENERATED_TRIGGERS` is at git-cicd:44, and install.sh has `TRIGGERS` at install.sh:40.

## Scope
1. New templates/workflows/cron.yml, workflow name `Cron`. Its `on:` is filled by `__SCHEDULE__`, the only part of any generated file that varies with the config.
   - The job that runs scripts gets write permissions as on Merge (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`), with `fetch-depth: 0` and `fetch-tags: true`. Decide and report get `statuses: write`.
   - No `${{ }}` inside `run:`. A header comment in open.yml's style.
2. DECISION (config with no cron job): `generate` writes no git-cicd-cron.yml and removes an existing one (printing it, as it does for the legacy file). `verify` fails while that file exists with no cron job declared. install.sh lists in the manifest only the generated files that exist after `generate` (the cron template is still always installed). Reason: GitHub requires at least one event under `on:`, and the doc forbids a schedule that never has anything to run.
3. `decide --trigger cron --cron=<expr>`, where the fired expression comes from `github.event.schedule` through an `env:` entry, quoted in `run:` like the other facts.
   - The needed runs are every (job, branch) pair whose job has cron in `on` and whose `cron` equals the fired expression, for each of its literal `branches`. `paths` do not apply; the reason is 'scheduled <expr>'.
   - Other cron jobs are 'not needed (scheduled at <their expr>)'.
   - DECISION: decide resolves each branch's head commit once, from `origin/<branch>` after a full checkout, and records it, so every job on a branch runs on the same commit. A branch that does not exist is reported as failed with 'branch <b> does not exist' and fails the verdict, never silently.
   - The decide outputs for the cron matrix are a list of {job, branch, sha}. DECISION: a cron-only output name, so the open outputs (and git-cicd-open.yml) stay unchanged.
4. DECISION: the CICD_ variables on cron are:
   - CICD_TRIGGER=cron
   - CICD_TARGET_BRANCH = CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH = the branch
   - CICD_BASE = CICD_HEAD = that branch's head commit
   - CICD_CHANGED_FILES = an empty file

   Reason: a schedule has no change.
5. Verdict: one `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` commit status on the head commit of each branch the run is for, pending first and final last, under the no-open-pull-request rule from gcd-bbdd.1. DECISION: `report` can produce a verdict per branch (for example one verdict file per branch holding the sha, state and description, which the status step loops over). The exact mechanism is left to the implementation, under the injection rules.
6. DECISION: cron runs do not join the Merge/Manual queue. Reason: a schedule event runs on the default branch's ref, not the job's branch, and the one cron job planned, the weekly update, only opens pull requests. The README documents this.
7. `verify` fails when the schedule block and the config disagree (the whole-file compare already does this; add a test).
8. install.sh `TRIGGERS` and `GENERATED_TRIGGERS` gain cron. This repository declares no cron job until the own-jobs issue, so no git-cicd-cron.yml is committed here.

## Tests (follow tests/test_workflow.py, tests/test_decide.py, tests/test_run.py, tests/test_report.py, tests/test_install.py)
- Schedule entries: one per distinct expression, sorted and quoted.
- No cron job: no file, and an existing file is removed; verify fails while it is there.
- A stale schedule block fails verify.
- decide picks only the jobs of the fired expression, on each branch; a missing branch fails.
- The cron CICD_ variables.
- One verdict per branch.
- No `${{ }}` in `run:`.
- git-cicd-open.yml is byte-identical.
- The install manifest.

## Docs
- README.md:
  - 'When a job runs' gains a cron bullet;
  - 'What a script is given';
  - the generated workflows table, plus a 'The cron workflow (Cron)' section: the schedule block, the no-cron-job handling, no queue, and that GitHub runs schedules only from the default branch's copy of the file;
  - the Commands table (`--cron`);
  - 'Not built yet'.
- AGENTS.md: the generated workflows list.

## Acceptance criteria
- `decide`, `run-job` and `report` run for cron, and nothing answers 'not built yet' any more.
- `generate` writes git-cicd-cron.yml with one schedule entry per distinct expression when a cron job exists, and handles the no-cron-job case as decided.
- `verify` fails on a hand edit or a stale schedule block.
- Every cron run ends with one Verdict status per branch head (or FAILED for a missing branch). A run that dies leaves the status pending or failed, never green.
- The suite passes on Python 3.11, `./git-cicd check` passes, and `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/<pr target>` reports nothing.

title: git-cicd's own release, vendor check and weekly update become git-cicd jobs
body:
Epic gcd-bbdd, planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gcd-bbdd.md (What ships: 'git-cicd's own release, vendor check and weekly update are git-cicd jobs'). Delivers into plan/git-dev-883c. Depends on gcd-bbdd.1 (merge), gcd-bbdd.2 (manual), gcd-bbdd.3 (declared inputs) and gcd-bbdd.4 (cron).

## What it replaces (do NOT add, change or delete these vendor-protected files; the planning session removes them from the integration branch later)
- .github/workflows/version-bump.yml ('Bump & Release'): runs on push to main and on a manual run with `bump_type`, `subdirectory` and `changelog_description`.
  - Job `bump` runs `python3 .vendored/pkg/git-semver/release bump`, skipped when the head commit message starts with `chore: bump version` or `chore: install`.
  - Job `publish` runs `release publish` when it starts with `chore: bump version`.
  - `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`; concurrency group push-to-main.
  - Environment: GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE, INPUT_BUMP_TYPE, INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY, INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION.
- .github/workflows/check-vendor.yml ('Check Vendor Files'): on every pull request, `python3 .vendored/check`. .vendored/check reads GITHUB_BASE_REF / GITHUB_HEAD_REF, or takes `--base`, and falls back to `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.
- .github/workflows/install-vendored.yml ('Install Vendored'): cron `0 9 * * 1`, plus a manual run with `vendor` (default all), `version` (default latest) and `private`.
  - It runs `python3 .vendored/install "$VENDOR" --version "$VERSION" --pr --deps=install`, adding `--private` when private is true.
  - Environment: GITHUB_TOKEN, VENDOR_PAT, and GH_TOKEN = VENDOR_PAT or else github.token.
- .vendored/pkg/git-semver/release reads GITHUB_EVENT_NAME (push or workflow_dispatch), GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE, GITHUB_SHA, GITHUB_REF, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, INPUT_BUMP_TYPE (default patch), INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY, INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION and GH_TOKEN.

## Scope
1. .vendored/configs/git-cicd.json declares three jobs beside `test`:
   - `release`: name 'Release', on [merge], branches [main], no paths, steps [ci/release.sh].
     - Inputs: `bump_type` (choices patch, minor, major; default patch), `subdirectory` (default empty), `changelog_description` (default empty), following the gcd-bbdd.3 design.
     - DECISION: no `paths`, so a push that changes only needs_nothing files does not release. Reason: a `chore: bump version` commit still triggers publish, because VERSION is in no job's paths and not in needs_nothing.
   - `vendor-check`: name 'Check Vendor Files', on [open], branches ['**'], no paths, steps [ci/vendor-check.sh].
   - `update-vendored`: name 'Install Vendored', on [cron], cron `0 9 * * 1`, branches [main], steps [ci/update-vendored.sh].
     - Inputs: `vendor` (default all), `version` (default latest), `private` (choices true, false; default false).
2. ci/release.sh (executable):
   - On CICD_TRIGGER=manual it sets GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=workflow_dispatch and runs `release bump`.
   - On merge it reads the subject of CICD_HEAD (`git log -1 --format=%s "$CICD_HEAD"`):
     - `chore: bump version...` runs `release publish`;
     - `chore: install...` prints that nothing is released and exits 0;
     - anything else runs `release bump` with GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push.
   - It exports GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE=$CICD_BASE, INPUT_BUMP_TYPE / INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY / INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION from the CICD_INPUT_ variables, and GH_TOKEN=$GITHUB_TOKEN.
   - It calls `python3 .vendored/pkg/git-semver/release` through an argv, never an eval.
3. ci/vendor-check.sh runs `python3 .vendored/check --base "$CICD_BASE"`. DECISION: it sets GITHUB_HEAD_REF from CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH when that is unset, so a local `check` and Actions both let chore/install-* branches through.
4. ci/update-vendored.sh runs `python3 .vendored/install "$CICD_INPUT_VENDOR" --version "$CICD_INPUT_VERSION" --pr --deps=install`, adding `--private` when CICD_INPUT_PRIVATE is true. It exports GH_TOKEN as VENDOR_PAT when set, else GITHUB_TOKEN. A session never runs this script or .vendored/install itself; only CI does.
5. .vendored/configs/git-semver.json (an editable vendor config): `files` gains templates/workflows/merge.yml, templates/workflows/cron.yml and templates/workflows/manual.yml.
6. Run `./git-cicd generate` and commit all four .github/workflows/git-cicd-{open,merge,cron,manual}.yml. `verify` passes, and git-cicd-open.yml is byte-identical to before the epic.
7. Docs:
   - README.md: 'Not built yet' lists only what remains (secrets beyond GITHUB_TOKEN and VENDOR_PAT; an image or runtime per job); the trigger table; 'Developing git-cicd' describes the four jobs and their scripts.
   - AGENTS.md: the generated workflows list, the jobs, and how to start the update and release by hand (Actions, Manual, job update-vendored / release with inputs JSON). Say truthfully that on the integration branch the old vendor workflows still exist next to the new jobs until the planning session removes them; nothing on main changes.

## Tests
- tests/: a test that this repository's config validates and declares test, release, vendor-check and update-vendored with the inputs above (in the style of `test_this_repository_is_migrated`).
- Tests must not run .vendored/install or the git-semver release.

## Acceptance criteria
- The config declares test, release, the vendor check and the update job. `./git-cicd validate` passes.
- All four generated workflows are committed and `./git-cicd verify` passes.
- The pull request into plan/git-dev-883c shows the row `Open / Check Vendor Files / git-cicd:vendor-check` and a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- version-bump.yml, check-vendor.yml and install-vendored.yml are untouched.
- The suite passes on Python 3.11, `./git-cicd check` passes, and `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.
